pergunta: Quando um exame pendente vira alerta?
referencia: Exames de urgencia pendentes ha mais de 6 horas e exames de rotina pendentes ha mais de 48 horas. [PROT-007]
base:
No sistema de gestão de exames médicos, quando um exame pendente é convertido em alerta, geralmente ocorre por uma das seguintes razões:

1. O exame foi realizado e está sendo processado.
2. O resultado do exame está disponível para consulta.
3. A data prevista para o retorno do resultado foi atingida.

O sistema notifica o médico sobre este status alterado através de notificações ou mensagens de texto, dependendo da configuração do hospital.

Para obter mais detalhes específicos sobre como funciona na sua instituição, recomendo entrar em contato diretamente com o departamento de tecnologia de informação ou com o setor responsável pelo gerenciamento de exames. pergunta: How to diagnose What I need to know about Crohn's Disease ?
referencia: A doctor will perform a physical exam and tests to diagnose Crohns disease. During your visit, the doctor will ask about your symptoms and medical history. The doctor may order blood tests, which involve drawing blood at a health care providers office or commercial facility and sending the sample to a lab for analysis. Blood tests can show anemia caused by bleeding. Anemia is a condition in which red blood cells are fewer or smaller than normal, which means less oxygen is carried to the bodys cells. Blood tests can also show a high white blood cell count, a sign of chronic inflammation. You may also be asked for a stool sample. A stool test is commonly used to rule out other causes of GI diseases, such as infections. The doctor will give you a container for catching and storing the stool. The sample is returned to the doctor or a commercial facility and sent to a lab for analysis. A stool sample can also be used to check if you have bleeding or inflammation. Other tests may be needed to diagnose Crohn's disease. The following tests are all performed at a hospital or outpatient center. - Colonoscopy. Colonoscopy is the most commonly used test to specifically diagnose Crohns disease. This test is used to look inside your rectum, entire colon, and ileum. The health care provider will give you written bowel prep instructions to follow at home before the test. You may need to follow a clear liquid diet for 1 to 3 days before the test.
base:
Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, but most commonly affects the small intestine called the ileum. The symptoms may include abdominal pain and cramping, diarrhea, fatigue, weight loss, fever, and rectal bleeding.

Diagnosis typically involves:

1. Medical history and physical examination.
2. Endoscopy: A procedure where a thin tube with a camera attached (endoscope) is inserted into the body to examine the inside of organs such as the intestines.
3. Biopsy: Taking a sample of tissue for laboratory analysis.
4. Imaging tests like CT scan, MRI, or ultrasound to look at the digestive tract.
5. Blood tests to check for inflammation markers and other potential issues.

Treatment usually includes medications to reduce inflammation, antibiotics if there's an infection, and sometimes surgery in severe cases. Early diagnosis and treatment are important to manage symptoms and prevent complications.
ajustado: What is the treatment for Crohn's disease? Treatment of Crohn's disease depends on the severity and location of symptoms, as well as whether complications have developed. The goal of treatment is to relieve symptoms and prevent complications. Medications may be used alone or in combination to treat Crohn's disease. These medications include antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, immunosuppressants, and biologic therapies. Antibiotics are used to treat infections caused by bacteria that can lead to diarrhea and abdominal pain. Anti-inflammatory drugs reduce inflammation and swelling in the intestines. Immunosuppressants suppress the immune system so it cannot attack healthy cells. Biologic therapies target specific proteins involved in inflammation and infection. Surgery may be needed if complications develop such as intestinal blockage, fistulas, abscesses, or severe bleeding.

These tests can help identify any abnormalities in organ positioning that may be associated with this condition. Additionally, physical examination by a physician can sometimes reveal signs of situs inversus, but these findings alone are not sufficient for a definitive diagnosis. A detailed history and thorough clinical evaluation from a specialist like an interventional radiologist or cardiologist who has experience with complex cases involving congenital anomalies can provide more accurate diagnostic insights.

pergunta: Is von Hippel-Lindau syndrome inherited ?

Unlike most autosomal dominant conditions, in which one altered copy of a gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the disorder, two copies of the VHL gene must be altered to trigger tumor and cyst formation in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome. A mutation in the second copy of the VHL gene occurs during a person's lifetime in certain cells within organs such as the brain, retina, and kidneys. An inability to repair DNA damage probably underlies the sun sensitivity in affected individuals. Mutations in at least one gene, MPLKIP, have been reported to cause a non-photosensitive form of trichothiodystrophy. Mutations in this gene account for fewer than 20 percent of all cases of non-photosensitive trichothiodystrophy. Little is known about the protein produced from the MPLKIP gene, although it does not appear to be involved in DNA repair. It is unclear how mutations in the MPLKIP gene lead to the varied features of trichothiodystrophy. In some cases, the genetic cause of trichothiodystrophy is unknown.

3. Insertions: Addition of one or more nucleotides within the gene.

pergunta: What is (are) Broken Heart Syndrome ?
referencia: Broken heart syndrome is a condition in which extreme stress can lead to heart muscle failure. The failure is severe, but often short-term. Most people who experience broken heart syndrome think they may be having a heart attack, a more common medical emergency caused by a blocked coronary (heart) artery. The two conditions have similar symptoms, including chest pain and shortness of breath. However, theres no evidence of blocked coronary arteries in broken heart syndrome, and most people have a full and quick recovery. Overview Broken heart syndrome is a recently recognized heart problem. It was originally reported in the Asian population in 1990 and named takotsubo cardiomyopathy (KAR-de-o-mi-OP-ah-thee). In this condition, the heart is so weak that it assumes a bulging shape (tako tsubo is the term for an octopus trap, whose shape resembles the bulging appearance of the heart during this condition). Cases have since been reported worldwide, and the first reports of broken heart syndrome in the United States appeared in 1998. The condition also is commonly called stress-induced cardiomyopathy. The cause of broken heart syndrome is not fully known. In most cases, symptoms are triggered by extreme emotional or physical stress, such as intense grief, anger, or surprise. Researchers think that the stress releases hormones that stun the heart and affect its ability to pump blood to the body.
base:
Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo cardiomyopathy, is an uncommon condition that can cause sudden chest pain and changes in the size of the left ventricle, which is the main pumping chamber of the heart. It's often triggered by emotional stress, such as grief or extreme joy, but it can occur after other stressful events like surgery or childbirth.

The term "broken heart" comes from the appearance of the left ventricular wall on X-rays, which resembles the shape of a tako (a Japanese octopus trap), hence the name "takotsubo." This condition affects women more frequently than men.

Symptoms include:
- Chest pain
- Shortness of breath
- Fatigue

It usually resolves within weeks to months without lasting damage to the heart muscle. However, it's important for healthcare providers to monitor patients closely because some people may have underlying heart conditions that could be exacerbated during this episode.
ajustado: Broken heart syndrome, also known as stress cardiomyopathy and takotsubo cardiomyopathy, is an acute condition that causes the heart to suddenly weaken and pump poorly. It usually occurs after a stressful event such as a severe emotional trauma, major surgery, or a serious illness. The symptoms of broken heart syndrome can be similar to those of coronary artery disease, including chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, fainting, and fatigue. However, unlike coronary artery disease, there is no blockage in the arteries supplying blood to the heart muscle. In most cases, the cause of broken heart syndrome is unknown.

pergunta: What is (are) Diabetic Nerve Problems ?
referencia: If you have diabetes, your blood glucose, or blood sugar, levels are too high. Over time, this can damage the covering on your nerves or the blood vessels that bring oxygen to your nerves. Damaged nerves may stop sending messages, or may send messages slowly or at the wrong times. This damage is called diabetic neuropathy. Over half of people with diabetes get it. Symptoms may include - Numbness in your hands, legs, or feet - Shooting pains, burning, or tingling - Nausea, vomiting, constipation, or diarrhea - Problems with sexual function - Urinary problems - Dizziness when you change positions quickly Your doctor will diagnose diabetic neuropathy with a physical exam and nerve tests. Controlling your blood sugar can help prevent nerve problems, or keep them from getting worse. Treatment may include pain relief and other medicines. People with AF can have multiple strokes, including silent strokes (strokes that don't show physical symptoms but show up on a brain scan) that, over time, can cause dementia, so prevention is important.

base: Yes, geleophysic dysplasia is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder. This means that if one parent has the condition, there's a 50% chance their child will inherit and develop the disease.

pergunta: What are the genetic changes related to leukoencephalopathy with brainstem and spinal cord involvement and lactate elevation ?
referencia: LBSL is caused by mutations in the DARS2 gene, which provides instructions for making an enzyme called mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase. This enzyme is important in the production (synthesis) of proteins in cellular structures called mitochondria, the energy-producing centers in cells. While most protein synthesis occurs in the fluid surrounding the nucleus (cytoplasm), some proteins are synthesized in the mitochondria. During protein synthesis, in either the mitochondria or the cytoplasm, building blocks (amino acids) are connected together in a specific order, creating a chain of amino acids that forms the protein. Mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase plays a role in adding the amino acid aspartic acid at the proper place in mitochondrial proteins. Mutations in the DARS2 gene result in decreased mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase enzyme activity, which hinders the addition of aspartic acid to mitochondrial proteins. It is unclear how the gene mutations lead to the signs and symptoms of LBSL. Researchers do not understand why reduced activity of mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase specifically affects certain parts of the brain and spinal cord.
